A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same diffusion-based chip-placement work. All pages, including v1's Appendices A–B and v2's Appendix A, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. The substantial methodological and experimental revisions can be compared reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-placement experiments, model and guidance ablations, and IBM/Adaptec benchmark results, with additional placement visualizations in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 reports original synthetic-data sensitivity studies, architecture ablations, clustered IBM placement experiments, and mixed-size placement results across 18 IBM circuits.

M1.justification: v2 replaces fixed-weight gradient guidance with backward universal guidance that optimizes predicted clean placements and adapts the legality weight through constrained optimization. The largest architecture changes from two blocks with three layers to three blocks with two layers, increasing parameters from 4.60M to 6.29M. The downstream procedure now fixes macros during DREAMPlace refinement, and synthetic generation introduces circuit-specific scale sampling and scale-dependent edge multipliers.

E1.justification: Real-circuit evaluation drops Adaptec1–4 and expands from ibm01–04 and ibm06 to ibm01–18, including the previously excluded standard-cell-only ibm05. Synthetic coverage broadens from SynthM/SynthM-Short/SynthL to distributions spanning variable edge-length scales, with additional tests across graph densities, circuit sizes, and sigmoid/linear edge-generation distributions. These changes alter represented circuits and distribution-shift scenarios, beyond dataset renaming.

E2.justification: v1 Table 8 compares the proposed method only with DREAMPlace. v2 Table 5 retains DREAMPlace and adds evaluated MaskPlace + DP, WireMask-BBO + DP, and ChiPFormer + DP comparisons. DREAMPlace also becomes a numerical comparator in the clustered-circuit evaluation in Table 4.

E3.justification: Real-circuit evaluation changes from an unfine-tuned Medium model with movable macros to two-stage synthetic training and fixed macros. Fine-tuning increases from 100k to 250k steps, the noise schedule changes from linear to cosine, dataset sizes change, and v2's architecture experiments specify 1M steps. Legality's boundary accounting changes, and optimizer-iteration evaluation disappears. v2 also specifies substituting the smallest corresponding row scores when aggregating WireMask-BBO failures.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the earlier pre-training analysis into systematic edge-count, vertex-count, scale, and edge-distribution studies, including clumping examples (Figures 4–7 and Table 2). It adds dataset/guidance comparisons on clustered IBM circuits. Architecture ablations remain, but attention is now described as replaced with graph convolutions. The earlier separate legality-only guidance control and Adaptec visual case studies disappear.

E5.justification: v1 Section 5.4 describes five runs using seed 1000, and Table 8 includes unexplained plus/minus quantities for the proposed method. v2 Table 5 instead specifies averages over five seeds and omits dispersion estimates. This changes seed and uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase in repetitions; neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced under changed conditions. For example, ibm06 changes from 5.77 versus DREAMPlace's 5.94 in v1 to 8.31 versus 6.15 in v2, reversing the ranking; all values are HPWL in millions. v2 Table 5 reports averages of 22.7 versus 23.6 across 18 IBM circuits, while Table 4 adds guided clustered-placement legality of 0.9970. New sensitivity results replace earlier synthetic tables, and iteration results disappear. These are not controlled cross-version performance comparisons.

T1.justification: v2 Section 4.3 adds a constrained HPWL objective, its Lagrangian, and mathematical updates for adaptive guidance. Section 3.2 also changes legality's numerator from the union of wholly in-bounds objects to the portion of the union inside the boundary. The underlying graph and DDPM definitions remain, and neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 adds Dataset Design as a central contribution: identifying transfer-critical synthetic-data parameters and designing distributions accordingly. v1 foregrounds architecture and data generation without this broader design-study claim. Synthetic-only zero-shot transfer remains central, but the introduction's benchmark claim narrows from IBM and Adaptec to IBM, and the abstract explicitly emphasizes guidance as the optimization alternative to RL.

C2.justification: v2 develops explanations linking sparse graphs to restricted information propagation and scale mismatch to clumping or excessive wirelength. It newly qualifies DREAMPlace's suitability for clustered circuits and discusses missing multimodal realism and test-time optimization tradeoffs. v1's explicit guidance-distribution limitation, final-optimizer dependence, and initialization/convergence interpretations are removed or substantially reframed.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix A documents guidance optimizers, learning rates, initialization, ten inner steps, tolerance, and a 1000-step diffusion schedule, alongside revised architecture and synthetic-generation parameters. The main text newly specifies hMetis, 512 clusters, cluster pin/net/area construction, and DREAMPlace 4.1. Conversely, the ArtNetGen/ASAP7/Cadence recipe, explicit training/validation splits, and Appendix B's benchmark statistics are removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds WireMask-BBO discussion and a hypergraph-partitioning citation, while removing references associated with ArtNetGen, ASAP7, and the dropped benchmark material. CircuitTraining's characterization changes from emphasizing failed PPA optimization and ordering volatility to acknowledging strong results while criticizing initialization dependence and online cost. Most of the existing research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: synthetic generation precedes architecture, experiments begin with dataset design, and scaling and architecture ablations are consolidated. Limitations are integrated into the conclusion, Appendix B disappears, and the abstract, contributions, and related work are rewritten. The title and author information change, and impact and acknowledgement sections are added.

P2.justification: The main text switches from one to two columns. The architecture and generation diagrams are retained with updates and exchanged numbering, while new sensitivity plots, clumping examples, and IBM workflow panels substantially change the visual evidence. Tables consolidate scaling and ablations and expand baseline comparisons while dropping iteration, percentage-change, and dispersion columns. Appendix B's benchmark table and Adaptec panels are removed.

improvement.justification: v1's competitive-placement claims relied on a DREAMPlace-only comparison, with limited evidence explaining synthetic-data transfer. v2's systematic dataset-design study, 18-circuit IBM comparison with three additional methods, and fixed-macro evaluation substantially strengthen evidence for generalization and downstream utility. Added guidance and clustering details improve reproducibility. Removing Adaptec coverage, dispersion estimates, and iteration measurements weakens breadth and statistical/runtime support, but the central evidential gains outweigh these losses.
